texts.preamble: Ram Saran vs State Of Haryana on 3 May, 2023 Neutral Citation No:=2023:PHHC Crr No.1054 of 2008 Neutral Citation No.2023:PHHC:063673 In The High Court Of Punjab And Haryana At Chandigarh Crr No.1054 of 2008 Date of Decision: May 03, 2023 Ram Saran ...Petitioner Versus State of Haryana ...Respondent Coram: Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Deepak Gupta Present: - Mr. Ashit Malik, Advocate for the petitioner. Mr. Parveen Kumar Aggarwal, Dag, Haryana. Deepak Gupta, J. This revision is against the order dated 17.1.2007 of conviction recorded by the trial Court, which has been affirmed by the Appellate Court on 28.5.2008. 2.
texts.facts: Brief facts, relevant to the case are that shop of the petitioner was inspected by Food Inspector on 22.12.1994 at about 3.30 PM and sample of khoya was taken, which on analysis was found to be adulterated. 3. Before this Court, short submission made by learned counsel for the petitioner is to reduce the sentence of the petitioner for the period already undergone by him, having regard to his advanced age and protracted trial. It Page No.1 out of 6 pages 1 of 6 Neutral Citation No:=2023:PHHC:063673 CRR No.1054 of 2008 Neutral Citation No.2023:PHHC:063673 is pointed out by learned counsel that against the minimum prescribed standard of 20% milk fat, the sample was found to contain Ram Saran vs State Of Haryana on 3 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/31043741/ 1 19.5% milk fat i.e., only 0.5% deficiency. Offence was committed in December, 1994 and a period of almost 29 years has elapsed and by this time, petitioner is more than 70 years of age. He has remained in custody from 28.05.2008 till his sentence was suspended by this Court vide order dated 03.06.2008. Accused was an old man suffering from asthma with clean past record.
texts.arguments: 4. Learned State Counsel, on the other hand submits that minimum sentence is provided for committing the offence under the provisions of the Act. However, learned State Counsel is unable to controvert the factual position as pointed out as above and the fact that the petitioner has no criminal antecedents nor there is anything on record to show that he is involved in any criminal activity post-conviction. 27. Fifth, unlike in State of Haryana v. Raja Ram, (1973) 1 SCC 544: 1973 SCC (Cri) 428 and Thakorlal D. Vadgama v. State of Gujarat, (1973) 2 SCC 413: 1973 SCC (Cri) 835, there is no grotesque misuse of power, wealth, status or age which needs to be guarded against.
